permutationLabel: Cardiovascular disease on dual antiplatelets (coronary stent 2 months ago)
summary: 69-year-old man with a drug-eluting coronary stent 2 months ago on aspirin and clopidogrel; melaena, HR 98, SBP 118, Hb 7.6, urea 13.1. Transfusion threshold is 8 g/dL with cardiovascular disease; antiplatelet management is a clinician/cardiology decision.

inputs.hpi: Three days of black tarry stools, now short of breath walking upstairs. Had a heart attack two months ago treated with a drug-eluting stent; takes aspirin and clopidogrel. No haematemesis. No NSAIDs. No chest pain today.

exam.general: Pale. Pulse 98/min regular, BP 118/72. No signs of heart failure.

comorbidities: Ischaemic heart disease — NSTEMI 2 months ago, drug-eluting stent

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute upper GI bleed on dual antiplatelet therapy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute upper GI bleed (melaena), Glasgow-Blatchford 11, on aspirin and clopidogrel after coronary stent 2 months ago. Cardiovascular disease: transfusion threshold Hb 8 g/dL. Antiplatelet plan with cardiology.

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: PANE top 3: inguinal hernia, cholecystitis, GORD. PANE never receives haematemesis/melaena: socrates-to-features has no answer rule for melaena, haematemesis, "vomiting blood" or coffee-ground vomit, and the "Upper GI bleed" CC hint sets only nausea_vomiting. With only epigastric_pain + nausea_vomiting, the male ×5 (×1.8 at ≥50) inguinal-hernia prior modifier or the cholecystitis/GORD priors win. Symptom inference and triageSurgical rank the bleed #1.
mustRankTopK.proposedFix: socrates-to-features.ts: add ASSOC/CC rules haematemesis|vomiting blood|coffee.?ground → haematemesis and melaena|black|tarry → melaena; also seed PANE from SmartSymptomPicker chips (HpiTab.reseedPane), not only the SOCRATES answers.

redFlags.note: Stopping DAPT within months of a drug-eluting stent risks stent thrombosis; continuing it risks rebleeding. The record must surface it for a clinician (and cardiology) decision.

mustInclude.note: ESGE: with acute or chronic cardiovascular disease, transfuse at Hb ≤8 g/dL, target ≥10 g/dL.
ESGE: do not interrupt aspirin for secondary prevention; P2Y12 inhibitor decisions with cardiology.

mustExclude.note: Unqualified advice to stop aspirin after a recent stent is contraindicated (ESGE: continue low-dose aspirin for secondary prevention; if interrupted, resume within 3–5 days).
Patient-directed stop/hold instructions are forbidden (hazard H-10); patient-facing text is linted separately (lint:patient-instructions).

mustExclude.knownGapNote: upper_gi_bleed protocol medications list "Tranexamic acid 1 g IV stat — if endoscopy is delayed and haemorrhage is trauma-related or massive"; it appears in every plan built on that protocol.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Remove tranexamic acid from the upper_gi_bleed protocol medications (ESGE 2021 recommends against it; HALT-IT). Surgeon sign-off needed.

guideline.name: ESGE Guideline — endoscopic diagnosis and management of nonvariceal upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage (NVUGIH), update 2021
guideline.section: Transfusion threshold Hb ≤8 g/dL (target ≥10) with cardiovascular disease; low-dose aspirin for secondary prophylaxis not interrupted (resume within 3–5 days if stopped); dual antiplatelet therapy — P2Y12 decision with cardiology
guideline.citation: Gralnek IM, Stanley AJ, Morris AJ, et al. Endoscopy. 2021;53:300–332.

guideline.name: BSG-led multisociety consensus care bundle — early clinical management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Restrictive transfusion: threshold 70 g/L, 80 g/L with cardiovascular disease
guideline.citation: Siau K, Hearnshaw S, Stanley AJ, et al. Frontline Gastroenterol. 2020;11:311–323.

guideline.name: NICE CG141 — Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding in over 16s: management
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG141. London: NICE; 2012 (last updated 2016).

guideline.name: HALT-IT randomised trial — tranexamic acid in gastrointestinal bleeding
guideline.section: Tranexamic acid: no benefit, more venous thromboembolism
guideline.citation: HALT-IT Trial Collaborators. Effects of a high-dose 24-h infusion of tranexamic acid on death and thromboembolic events in patients with acute gastrointestinal bleeding (HALT-IT). Lancet. 2020;395:1927–1936.

rationale: Permutation: cardiovascular disease and dual antiplatelets after a recent stent. Tests the higher transfusion threshold (8 g/dL), that the antiplatelets are flagged for a clinician/cardiology decision, and that no engine gives a blanket "stop aspirin" instruction.

authoring.author: Claude (upper-GI cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Citations written from the guideline texts, not yet checked against the source (verified: false).
